newsitem.title: UK: Russian Eurobonds rally on debt deal hopes.
newsitem.headline: Russian Eurobonds rally on debt deal hopes.

text.p: Russian Eurobonds have rallied on hopes that a London Club debt rescheduling agreement is closer, bankers said on Wednesday.
"The Russian rally is being driven by credit improvement and progress towards the London Club rescheduling," Eric Fine, Russian and eastern Europe debt strategist at Morgan Stanley said.
The Russian Federation's benchmark 2007 dollar bond was trading at 320 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, down from 349 a week ago and 375 when launched in June.
Since the issue, there has been speculation that Russia might be upgraded this year.
Its 2001 dollar paper was quoted at 245 b.p. over, from 267 a week ago. The $1.0 billion deal was issued at a 345 b.p. launch spread last November.

Bankers said Russia was meeting London Club of commercial bank creditors on Wednesday and could propose to lower the threshold necessary to close its debt restructuring agreement to 75 percent from 90 percent.
Although the banks might be reluctant to accept this level, they could agree to a lower limit of 80 to 85 percent, dealers said.
Last week Russia said it planned to announce a closing agreement schedule with the London Club creditors by late September.

The market was also increasingly bullish on Russia's ratings outlook. Rating agencies Moody's and Standard & Poor's are expected to review their long-term foreign currency debt ratings later this year.
"Russia is expected to at least receive a change in its ratings outlook, even if an upgrade is not given this year," Fine at Morgan Stanley said.
Russia is rated Ba2 by Moody's, and BB minus by S&P with a stable outlook. Both ratings were awarded in October of last year.
Analysts said Russia's chances of getting a sovereign credit upgrade were slim, but economic and fiscal improvements since October could lead to a change in outlook to positive from stable.

On Tuesday an S&P official, when asked about Russia's chances for an upgrade, said Russia faced severe fiscal challenges, and the question was whether there had been a fundamental and radical change since October.
Other Russian Eurobonds have also tightened. The City of Moscow issued a $500 million three-year bond in May at 315 b.p. over Treasuries. It was quoted at around 260 b.p. over on Wednesday.
The City of St Petersburg's $300 million five-year bond launched in June was the exception, an was holding close to its 312.5 b.p. launch spread.
